facts.raw_span: A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
intermittent generalized pruritus
blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri
bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa
no granulomas or malignant cells were identified
A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
intermittent generalized pruritus
blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri
bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa
no granulomas or malignant cells were identified

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, sclerotic changes, and histiocytic infiltration with foamy histiocytes and Touton-like giant cells is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease.

The patient's radiographic findings of sclerotic changes and uptake in long bones could be seen in Langerhans cell histiocytosis, although the absence of CD1a and langerin staining makes this less likely.
The patient's presentation of elevated inflammatory markers and enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland could be seen in sarcoidosis, although the absence of granulomas makes this less likely.
The patient's radiographic findings of sclerotic changes and uptake in long bones could be seen in bone metastasis, although the absence of malignant cells makes this less likely.
The patient's radiographic findings of sclerotic changes could be seen in Paget's disease of bone, although the absence of characteristic deformities makes this less likely.
The patient's radiographic findings of sclerotic changes could be seen in osteopetrosis, although the absence of characteristic fractures makes this less likely.

The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain and histiocytic infiltration could be seen in multicentric reticulohistiocytosis, although the absence of characteristic skin lesions makes this less likely.
The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain and histiocytic infiltration could be seen in Rosai-Dorfman disease, although the absence of characteristic lymphadenopathy makes this less likely.
